claims.text: Purchases of taxed beverages decreased by an average of 6% (-12 mL/capita/day) in 2014 relative to the counterfactual.
Purchases of taxed beverages decreased at an increasing rate up to a 12% decline by December 2014.
All three socioeconomic groups reduced purchases of taxed beverages following the tax implementation.
Reductions in purchases of taxed beverages were higher among low socioeconomic status households, averaging a 9% decline during 2014.
Purchases of taxed beverages among low socioeconomic status households decreased up to 17% by December 2014 compared with pretax trends.
Purchases of untaxed beverages were 4% (36 mL/capita/day) higher than the counterfactual in 2014.
The increase in untaxed beverage purchases was mainly driven by an increase in purchases of bottled plain water.

methodologies.name: Difference in difference fixed effects model
methodologies.description: Used a difference in difference fixed effects model adjusting for macroeconomic variables and pre-existing trends to compare observed 2014 beverage purchase volumes against a counterfactual based on pretax trends.
datasets: Unbalanced panel of 6253 households providing 205 112 observations in 53 Mexican cities
conditions: Excise tax on sugar sweetened beverages

future_work.text: Continued monitoring to understand longer-term beverage purchases, potential substitutions, and health implications.
